subject.title: feat: add disableBoundaryAwareCache compat option for prefix-matching prompt cache providers

question: Should OpenClaw adopt this public `compat.disableBoundaryAwareCache` contract with a DeepSeek-on default, or prefer the config-free policy proposed in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/94945?
rationale: Both branches address a real regression, but they establish different long-term provider and configuration contracts; repository policy requires explicit ownership of new config/default behavior rather than inferring that choice from technical correctness alone.

options.title: Adopt the DeepSeek-scoped compat policy
options.body: Merge this proven provider-scoped implementation after refreshing it against current main, and close the competing policy branch once exact-head validation passes.

options.title: Prefer the config-free sibling
options.body: Choose the broader implicit-prefix-provider behavior only after equivalent live provider proof and compatibility review, then close this PR as superseded.

options.title: Design an internal provider policy
options.body: Avoid a public config key by introducing a narrower internal provider capability only if owners conclude users should not control this behavior.

recommendation.title: Adopt the DeepSeek-scoped compat policy
recommendation.body: Merge this proven provider-scoped implementation after refreshing it against current main, and close the competing policy branch once exact-head validation passes.

likelyOwner.reason: This person is an official repository maintainer with recent history across the affected cache-boundary, provider-compatibility, and shared type surfaces.
